focus: A7 dual-key config and v1 tolerance probe: can one opencode.json plus one agent frontmatter carry both v1 and v2 keys without either version breaking or misreading them?

graphEvents.label: Can one set of agent, command, skill and opencode.json files serve both versions?
v1 hard-rejects the v2 permissions config key and invalidates the whole project
v1 forwards unknown agent frontmatter keys into provider options
v2 diverts sibling agent keys into request.body when permission: is present
v1 unwraps mcp.servers into real servers with enabled true
opencode2 debug agents is the v2 agent-registration oracle and follows the agents symlink

label: OpenCode v1 1.19.3 hard-rejects the v2 permissions config key with a purpose-built guard that invalidates the entire project config, so one opencode.json cannot carry both permission and permissions.
OpenCode v1 silently ignores the plugins (plural) config key: the declared package never loads, no warning is printed, and only the singular plugin array survives into the resolved config.

mcp.servers is the one v2 config shape v1 genuinely tolerates: v1 unwraps the servers level, promotes its children to real MCP servers and fills in enabled true, making mcp.servers.<name> the only MCP spelling proven safe on both hosts.

OpenCode v1 forwards unrecognised agent frontmatter keys into the agent provider options passthrough: permissions and disabled each appear twice, the second copy inside options, while steps, hidden and color are recognised first-class fields and do not leak.

OpenCode v2 mirrors the leak in the opposite direction: the presence of the v1 permission: key does not reject the agent but diverts permissions and disabled into request.body, the provider passthrough, instead of applying them as a Ruleset.

A shared agent frontmatter is viable only in the v1 shape plus the benign shared extras: description, mode, steps, hidden and color are accepted by both hosts, while permissions: and disabled: must never appear in a shared file.

OpenCode v2 reads the v1 permission map and translates it into a Permission.Ruleset, renaming the action bash to shell, so the v1 map is the portable permission spelling while resource-scoped deny and ask rules cannot be expressed in a shared file.

opencode2 debug agents is a real v2 agent-registration oracle returning 19 agents including the 12 repo project agents through the ancestor .opencode/agents symlink, resolving the v2-oracle asymmetry that iteration 7 could not find for commands.

Unknown keys on either host are never rejected at agent load time; they are relocated into that host provider passthrough, so frontmatter tolerance must be judged by where a key lands, not by whether loading succeeded.

direction: One opencode.json carrying both permission: (v1 map) and permissions: (v2 Ruleset) for per-version fidelity
reason: v1 rejects the document outright with a dedicated error and the project becomes unusable, so the dual spelling cannot be shipped even as a tolerated extra.

direction: Declaring plugins: (plural) in a shared opencode.json so v2 installs plugins while v1 ignores it
reason: v1 drops the key without any warning, producing an install that looks healthy but loads nothing; a silent no-op is not an acceptable compatibility strategy.
